title: The Justice of Eternal Punishment
english: They are opposing the laws that were given and the laws that are intended. We see this happening to us as well, in the way we instruct children, desiring to lead them up by way of knowledge so that they might practice this; but they do not always practice it as they were taught.

Rather, there are times when many sons, having been raised by doctors who were also fathers, do not use medicine properly, bringing disease-causing things instead of healthy ones to those who are suffering; and it is not the medicine, nor the one who trained it, who is the cause. For he did not teach so that they might act in this way. For they act not as they learned to act.

Again, we instruct certain laws so that they might establish the righteous and avoid injustice. But some of them, approaching the laws badly, do the opposite. And we blame neither the law nor the lawgiver. For if they themselves were the cause of injustice, they would not have punished the unjust. For this also is part of their will: that the unjust should be punished. And God punishes the devil, and those who have transgressed the laws set by God. For He says to certain evil ones: 'Go into the eternal fire, prepared for the devil and his angels' (Matt 25:41).

Therefore, let those who oppose these things know that they fight against themselves. For if the devil were essentially evil and a stranger to the good God, being able to be his equal in strength, he would not have prepared a punishment for himself, nor would he be able to be cast into the punishment; but He says that fire is prepared for the devil. And this must be said: If the good God is unchangeable, as...

If it indeed exists, and always possesses the same power, not to be strong one way and then another; yet after much harm and much loss, it was destined to hand over the devil to the eternal fire. Why did he not do this from the beginning, when he returned to him and took part in him? For then, rather, punishment was being decreed against him as for a greater transgression. Now indeed he harms men; but then, against them, he harmed the divinity, as they think.

For law and righteous indignation are more appropriate against those daring against the king than against those who are subjects. For if these things are so thought, they will attribute either ignorance to God then, regarding how he will punish and obstruct evil, or weakness. But neither of these applies to the good God; so the enemy would not have returned against him unprovoked. Rather, having become to be good, he kept the power of virtue incomplete, but led the readiness of evil into activity; for which reason he is also worthy of punishment, and appropriately, after much punishment, was cast down.

If they were to bring forward that also, which was said by John the Baptist to those coming to baptism with hypocrisy: 'O generation of vipers, who showed you to flee from the coming wrath? Therefore make fruit worthy of repentance, and do not think to yourselves that we have Abraham as father. For God is able from these stones to raise children to Abraham. Already the axe lies at the root of the trees. Every tree therefore not producing good fruit is cut down, and into fire' (Matthew 3:7-10).
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The true father and the nature of scorpions
english: It is cast down. Let them hear that they are unable to bring forth [fruit] from those things which they do not accept. For they do not accept John the Baptist, who happens to be one of the Old Testament. However, it must even so be said to them: through all their opposition, he denies that things are good by nature and that things are evil by nature. For he says to them: 'Produce therefore fruit worthy of repentance' (Matt 3:8). But repentance and its fruit do not fall either toward the evil in essence or toward the good in nature. For how can the always-good need repentance? Or how can the evil by nature make use of the good of repentance? For he who is evil in essence is unable to turn away from sin; nor does repentance occur for the sake of the good.

Furthermore, concerning the stones, which are shown by him, he says children shall be raised up to Abraham (Matt 3:9); but by saying stones, he means the foolish, and still men remaining in wickedness. For if these were to repent and to believe in God, they would be children of Abraham, who because of this was counted a man of God, because he believed in God, as his faith was counted toward righteousness (Gen 15:6). And since we heard that also being said by them toward those born from Abraham and the other holy men, 'You breed of hedgehogs' (Matt 3:7), saying 'hedgehogs' signifies those around Abraham; let them know they are fighting against the sequence of the chapter. For he reproves them, as not being of Abraham, but offspring of hedgehogs, pretending and shouting to be of Abraham. For the Savior says in another chapter to them...

Abraham did not do this, though you lie, saying he is your father. For if you were children of Abraham, you would have done the works of Abraham. But you are from your own father, the devil, and you desire to do the desires of your own father. For he has been a manslayer from the beginning, and he does not stand in the truth (John 8:44). And it is well to say, 'He does not stand,' showing him previously standing in the truth.

He calls the devil their father, because of the similarity of manner and quality. Thus, he did not say that Abraham and the saints with him are scorpions. For he had this change, to be sons of scorpions, because they used evil men as teachers, according to their own choice. Thus John says to them: Since you desired to undergo a change from virtue to snakes—for such were not even less in essence—stop being offspring of scorpions (Matt 3:7), whose quality you desired to have. For evil comes from evil, and you strove to be unrighteous from the unrighteous.

But since, because you are coming to baptism, you say you bring a sign of repentance, yet you do this hypocritically, I say to you: Who showed you to flee from the coming wrath (Matt 3:10)? For the one repenting, repents for this reason: so that he may no longer flee from the wrath that is coming against those who sin. And 'Who showed you?' is inquired, so that he might say the one truly showing how to withdraw from wickedness does not make this happen hypocritically. But you do this with hypocrisy, coming to be baptized. Therefore, you will not be cleansed.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: True Children of Abraham and the Purpose of Punishment
english: For one desiring to be truly purified turns away from sins, and such a repentance bears fruit, performing works contrary to sin. But you have not done this, judging yourselves, claiming to have Abraham as a father. But it will not benefit you to merely know that you are children of Abraham, but to be his children through faith and flight from idols. Even if you have become children of Abraham at some point, this will not save you. For God is able to make those who are not currently his children into his children. Thus, the one who is a child of Abraham according to virtue is saved, not the one who became his child according to the flesh only; and if he does become [a child], let him not think much of it, for such a thing is transitory.

Indeed, those who do not have it will also be able to acquire it. For Paul, whom he did not beget according to the flesh, says: 'For in Christ I have begotten you through the Gospel' (Gal 4:15). But do not despise these things, as if the wrath against sinners were slow. For through this, the foolish man already has the punishment for sinning, being a subject to punishment. You know by this the axe already approaching the roots of the trees. He does not speak of actual trees, but of men composed of wickedness. The root of these trees is a corrupt disposition, from which the fruit becomes not edible, but poisonous. Therefore, he did not speak of a good fruit. If then the axe signifies the punishment, and the bad tree signifies the sinning man, these are not opposing natures; for the punishment threatens to fell the trees. For he who threatens the sinners intends to change them through that very threat.

If then, through the threat of the axe, which is about to cut down the rotten trees, he persuades them to stop bearing bad fruit and instead bear good, the tree is not naturally bad, nor is the punishment naturally bad. But perhaps they will say: 'If the punishment changes the foolish, it is good; but if the punishment is good, and the promise is contrary to it, and opposites cannot both be good, then the promise is bad.' But the punishment is not a bad thing, since the promise is good. If the punishment is bad, it is not God, but Satan who brings it. But Satan brings punishment not to his own; for they are, as he is, evil, and it is necessary even him to fall under punishment; so he would do it to good. But this is impossible; therefore, it is not the evil one who brings it, but God.

And everything brought by God is brought usefully, happening to be either a maker of good or a preventer of evil. Therefore, God, desiring to prevent evil, brings this; and he would not attempt to prevent evil if it were not possible to prevent evil. But this prevention cannot be something natural and ungenerated. And the ignorant have stumbled even here, thinking the punishment to be contrary to the promise; for each is a retribution: the one bringing reward to the good, and the other punishment against those who have voluntarily transgressed the divine laws.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
